content.text: K < 2.5 mEq/L: use IV K, not PO. Monitor K and adjust; recheck periodically during maintenance. Take w meals and a glass of water, ⍉ on an empty stomach (gastric irritation); swallow whole (⍉ crush, chew or suck). Doses > 40 mEq/day: divide so ≤ 40 mEq per dose. Hypokalemia: typically 40 to 100 mEq/day; maintenance or prophylaxis: typically 20 mEq/day. CI: triamterene or amiloride (severe hyperkalemia). Solid forms can cause ulcerative or stenotic GI lesions; consider liquid K in dysphagia or severe GI motility disorders. Severe vomiting, abd pain, distention or GI bleeding: stop and consider ulceration, obstruction or perforation. RAAS inhibitors (ACEi, ARB, spironolactone, eplerenone, aliskiren): closely monitor K; NSAIDs: closely monitor K.
